Position description The Department of Molecular and Medical Pharmacology at the University of California, Los Angeles invites applications for an Assistant Adjunct Professor position in the Adjunct Professor Series (non-tenure track). The successful candidate will conduct independent and collaborative research in molecular and medical pharmacology, with an emphasis on human stem cell and organoid models, disease mechanisms, and therapeutic discovery. Responsibilities include developing and applying human organoid systems, genome engineering approaches, genetic and pharmacologic perturbation strategies, functional genomics, and multi-omic approaches to identify disease mechanisms, validate therapeutic targets, and evaluate candidate interventions. Research activities will focus on diabetes and metabolic disease, with opportunities to extend these approaches to other diseases and organ systems. The candidate will be expected to participate in interdisciplinary collaborations, trainee mentorship, scientific publications, grant proposals/development, engage in teaching, and service activities consistent with the academic responsibilities of the Adjunct Professor series and the mission of the Department of Molecular and Medical Pharmacology. Position description Advanced Heart Failure and Transplant Cardiology Faculty Search The Cardiology Division of the University of California, San Francisco, is seeking a board-certified or eligible faculty candidate in advanced heart failure and transplant cardiology for its growing program. The successful candidate will join a comprehensive, multidisciplinary program that provides the full spectrum of advanced heart failure care, including heart transplantation, temporary and durable mechanical circulatory support (MCS), cardiogenic shock management, and pulmonary hypertension management. Clinical responsibilities include inpatient and outpatient care of advanced heart failure, transplant, and MCS patients; participation in multidisciplinary transplant and MCS patient selection committees; and teaching and mentoring of medical students, residents, and fellows, including trainees in the ACGME-accredited Advanced Heart Failure and Transplant Cardiology fellowship. Qualifications • Education & Rank: Must hold an MD, MD/PhD, or MD/MPH degree and qualify for appointment at the Instructor, Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor rank. • Clinical Training: Formal fellowship training in both inpatient and outpatient management of advanced heart failure, heart transplantation, temporary and durable mechanical circulatory support (MCS) devices, and pulmonary hypertension. • Board Certification: Board certification or eligibility in Cardiovascular Disease and in Advanced Heart Failure and Transplant Cardiology (ABIM). • Licensure: Possession of, or eligibility for, a medical license in the State of California. Position description Assistant (Tenure-Track) Professor in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (MAE) Faculty Position in Aero/Space Structures The Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering at the University of California, Irvine (UCI) is inviting applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the assistant professor rank, with an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027. The rapidly evolving landscape of aerospace engineering, driven by advances in next-generation aircraft, urban air mobility, hypersonic and high-speed vehicles, and ambitious space initiatives such as NASA’s Artemis program, the United States Space Force, and the growing commercial space sector, calls for pioneering innovations in aerospace and space structures. Future air and space platforms will demand structures that are lighter, stronger, more adaptable, and more efficient than conventional approaches allow, spanning applications from high-performance airframes to deployable, in-orbit, and lunar/planetary structures.. To address these challenges, UCI’s Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering seeks exceptional applicants with demonstrated potential to become a leader in aero/space structures. Areas of Interest span experimental, computational, and theoretical thrusts and include: • Advanced structural concepts for air and space platforms, including deployable, reconfigurable, and morphing structures (origami- and kirigami-inspired, thin-shell composite, and tensegrity concepts), in-space manufacturing, and in-space/in-field robotic, modular, and autonomous assembly and repair of large-scale structures. • Aerospace structures leveraging advanced composites and additive manufacturing, including AI-driven strategies for manufacturing, computational design and optimization, and adaptive or multifunctional structures with integrated actuation and sensing. • Structural mechanics and life-cycle assessment of aircraft and spacecraft structures with emphasis on materials behavior and characterization, including fatigue, fracture, and damage tolerance, aeroelasticity, and structural health monitoring across airframe and space-structure applications with extreme thermal, mechanical, and/or dynamic loading. • Emerging structural challenges in hypersonic, reusable, and autonomous platforms, including thermal-structural and aerothermoelastic response, and resilient, rapidly manufacturable structures for next-generation defense and space missions. • Structural dynamics of large, flexible, and ultralight space structures, including pointing-error mitigation under attitude-control maneuvers. For full consideration, applications should be submitted by December 15, 2026. This position will remain open until filled. Apply online at recruit.ap.uci.edu/JPF10461. Position description The Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering at the University of California, Irvine invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in multidisciplinary design and optimization (MDO), with an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027. We seek outstanding candidates advancing the theory, computation, and application of MDO for complex engineering systems, with particular emphasis on aerospace applications and AI-driven approaches. Advances in machine learning, high-performance computing, and digital engineering are reshaping how complex aerospace systems are designed. Design cycles that once proceeded sequentially, discipline by discipline, can now be posed as a single coupled problem, so that structural integrity, thermal management, aerodynamic performance, and propulsion efficiency are optimized simultaneously rather than reconciled after the fact. Areas of primary interest include AI-integrated aerospace vehicle design; digital engineering and autonomous system optimization; surrogate modeling for complex aero-thermal systems; and data-driven flight dynamics. Related areas include optimization of coupled multiphysics systems, reduced-order modeling, design under uncertainty and robust or reliability-based optimization, and model-based systems engineering. Candidates developing broadly applicable methodologies are encouraged to apply regardless of the specific application domain in which their work has been demonstrated. The successful candidate will establish a high-impact, externally funded research program; teach and mentor students at the undergraduate and graduate levels; and contribute to the intellectual life of the department and the profession. The position will strengthen the department’s systems and design area and provide opportunities for collaboration across dynamics and controls, fluid dynamics and propulsion, mechanics of materials and structures, and thermal and transport sciences, as well as across the Samueli School of Engineering and Southern California’s aerospace and technology community. Applications should be submitted at http://recruit.ap.uci.edu/JPF10462, the UCI Recruit portal. Documentation Required: Curriculum Vitae, Cover Letter, Statement of Research, Reflective Teaching Mentoring Statement, Publications (three publications or manuscripts), References (contact information only - 3 required). Position description The University of California, Berkeley invites applications for an approved faculty position at either the non-tenured (tenure-track) Assistant Professor level or the tenured Associate Professor level in the area of Electronic, Functional, and Quantum Materials. Rank will be determined based on qualifications and experience. This appointment will be a joint 50% Materials Science and Engineering / 50% Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences appointment. This appointment will start as a 100% Materials Science and Engineering (MSE) appointment, with the appointee joining the Bakar Institute for Digital Materials for the Planet (BIDMaP) in the College of Computing, Data Science, and Society (CDSS) as a member, with access to its collaborative resources and postdoctoral program. BIDMaP advances the synthesis, design, and translation of innovative materials aimed at mitigating critical global challenges. Through the integration of pioneering chemistry with machine learning, artificial intelligence, and robotic automation, BIDMaP transforms materials innovation into targeted solutions for clean air, clean water, advanced batteries, and sustainable chemical production. About the Position: We seek outstanding candidates demonstrating the potential to build a world-class research program that uses and advances AI to enable transformational progress in materials science and engineering. Research may span the development of new AI methods motivated by materials challenges, co-development of emergent AI with materials theory and experimentation, and the deployment of AI to accelerate materials research, discovery and innovation. Application areas are intentionally broad, encompassing the full breadth of materials science—from soft to hard matter and inorganic to organic systems—and all stages of the materials lifecycle, including synthesis, processing, modeling, theory, characterization, fabrication, integration, deployment, and reuse. jobs.description: Position overview Position title: Assistant Professor Salary range: $88,300-$114,400 Percent time: 100% FTE Anticipated start: July 1, 2027 or later Application Window Open date: October 6, 2026 Next review date: Friday, Nov 6, 2026 at 11:59pm (Pacific Time) Apply by this date to ensure full consideration by the committee. Position description The Department of Film and Media Studies at UC Santa Barbara invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Media Industries and AI. We seek a scholar whose research and teaching examines artificial intelligence as a media industry phenomenon, including its infrastructures, labor, political economy, regulation, and cultural, artistic, and social implications. We welcome candidates working on any global region and through any critical, historical, or empirical methodology, including but not limited to production studies, platform and infrastructure studies, science and technology studies, critical algorithm studies, political economy, labor studies, cultural and industrial history, and creative or practice-based research on generative media. We are especially interested in candidates who can speak to one or more of the following: the restructuring of film, television, gaming, digital media, and/or music industries by AI systems; the labor of AI production, from data annotation to creative and technical work displaced or transformed by automation; the environmental, material, and geopolitical infrastructures underlying AI; algorithmic culture, recommendation systems, and platform governance; or the aesthetics, authorship, and cultural politics of generative and synthetic media. This position calls for a humanities-based, critical, media industries approach to the study of AI—one attentive to history, culture, power, embodiment, and meaning-making, rather than a purely technical or computational orientation. We therefore welcome scholars whose work engages AI and media industries through racial, gender, queer, global and/or transnational, environmental, creative, and other critical approaches. Candidates for the position will be expected to teach in our core Film and Media Studies undergraduate and graduate curriculum, and to develop new courses—large lecture classes and smaller seminars—in their areas of expertise. They ideally will participate in existing research clusters and centers within our department, including the Carsey-Wolf Center and its Media Industries and AI Research Initiative, the Global Media Technologies and Cultures Lab, and Wireframe Studio, as well as those associated with other departments, programs, and centers on campus. The faculty of the Department of Film and Media Studies engages in scholarship and pedagogy across multiple scholarly approaches, fostering a dynamic and expansive understanding of film and media study. We are a robust department with over 500 undergraduate majors and 30 doctoral students. With this appointment, we seek to extend the department’s scholarly and curricular strengths and advance our department’s commitment to diverse, interdisciplinary research and teaching. Qualifications Basic qualifications (required at time of application) The minimum qualification to be considered for this position is the completion of all requirements for a PhD except the dissertation in Film and Media Studies or a related discipline at the time of application. Position description The Department of Plant Pathology in the College of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences at the University of California, Davis is recruiting an Assistant Professor of Plant Pathology with an emphasis on plant health and microbiomes. This is an academic year (9-month), tenure-track Assistant Professor position that includes an appointment in the California Agricultural Experiment Station (AES), with responsibility for research and outreach relevant to the AES mission, as well as university service. The appointee is expected to establish a competitive, externally funded research program in plant microbiome science that addresses critical and emerging issues in plant pathology. The program should advance microbiome-informed approaches to the diagnosis, prediction, and/or management of plant diseases and develop science-based solutions to promote plant health. Research should generate fundamental and applied understanding of the composition, function, and/or dynamics of plant-associated microbial communities (including bacteria, fungi, oomycetes, viruses, and/or other microorganisms) and their interactions with plant hosts and each other. Areas of interest may include disease-suppressive microbiomes, dysbiosis and pathobiomes, host-microbiome-pathogen interactions, pathogen-pathogen and pathogen-nonpathogen interactions, disease complexes and multi-infections, microbiome engineering, synthetic communities, and the ecology and evolution of pathogens within the phytomicrobiome. Research may also address climate-driven changes in plant-microbiome interactions and emerging diseases, span model, agricultural, and/or natural plant systems, and should have a strong mechanistic and/or predictive foundation. The appointee will complement existing departmental strengths in plant-microbe interactions, disease epidemiology, and disease management, while expanding microbiome-informed approaches relevant to food security, agricultural sustainability, climate resilience, and the broader One Health framework. The appointee will be expected to teach GDB103: The Microbiome of People, Animals and Plants, a 3-unit, upper-division undergraduate course that serves Global Disease Biology (GDB) and other students. The appointee is also expected to contribute to required GDB courses, such as GDB90: Introduction to Global Disease Biology, GDB 187: Global Disease Biology Seminar, and PMI129Y: One Health: Human, Animal & Environment Interfaces, and will have opportunities to contribute to graduate courses such as PLP201B: Ecology and Epidemiology of Plant Pathogenic Organisms and PLP298: Microbial Ecology. Training and mentoring of graduate students, undergraduate student advising, curricular development, outreach, and departmental and university service are expected. The successful candidate will be an active member of the Plant Pathology Graduate Program and other graduate groups as appropriate and will have opportunities to collaborate with Cooperative Extension specialists and advisors, relevant industries, and other public stakeholders. This recruitment is conducted at the Assistant Professor rank, and the resulting appointment will be at that rank regardless of the appointee's qualifications.

Position description The Department of Physics and Astronomy at the University of California, Davis invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor in hard condensed matter experimental physics. We seek candidates with an outstanding research record and the potential to establish a highly visible, externally funded program. Candidates from all areas of experimental condensed matter physics are encouraged to apply. Areas of interest include quantum materials and emergent phenomena; strongly correlated and topological systems; superconductivity and magnetism; low-dimensional, nanoscale, and mesoscopic systems; nonequilibrium and ultrafast phenomena; quantum transport and devices; and novel experimental techniques, instrumentation, or materials platforms. We especially welcome research that complements or expands existing strengths and fosters collaboration across UC Davis. The successful candidate will develop an independent, internationally recognized research program; teach effectively at the undergraduate and graduate levels; mentor students; contribute to the condensed matter community; and participate in departmental, university, and professional service. Candidates must have a Ph.D. or equivalent degree in physics or a closely related field by the time of application. UC Davis offers a collaborative environment with strengths in quantum materials, materials synthesis, spectroscopy, scanning probe microscopy, nuclear magnetic resonance, low-temperature physics, optical and transport measurements, nanostructures, and quantum phenomena, together with a strong condensed matter theory community and interdisciplinary connections across Materials Science and Engineering, Chemistry, Electrical and Computer Engineering, and other departments. Faculty have access to extensive shared infrastructure, including the Center for Nano-MicroManufacturing (CNM2), the Advanced Materials Characterization and Testing Laboratory (AMCaT), and a departmental helium recovery and liquefaction facility, as well as major national user facilities including the Advanced Light Source and Molecular Foundry at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and SSRL and LCLS at SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory. The successful candidate will join a mature experimental and theoretical condensed matter community while helping shape its next phase through new scientific directions, techniques, and capabilities. Position description The Department of Psychology and the Department of Urban Planning and Public Policy (UPPP) in the School of Social Ecology at the University of California, Irvine, invite applications for a joint tenure-track faculty position at the Associate Professor level in Behavior Change, Decision Science, and Policy. The position will advance research on how individuals and groups make decisions, change behavior, and respond to interventions, institutions, and public policy. We seek scholars who connect behavioral science to important real-world problems with a strong commitment to translating research into effective interventions, actionable programs, and policy solutions. The successful candidate will complement the Department of Psychology’s strengths in basic and applied behavioral research (spanning developmental, health, social, or clinical domains) as well as UPPP’s focus on public policy, inequality, social problems and environmental issues. Interdisciplinary Research and Policy We welcome scholars whose research examines behavior change and decision-making––such as motivation, beliefs, social influence, self-regulation, and risk perception––and connects them to policy design, practice, and broader societal outcomes. We are particularly interested in candidates who bridge individual-level psychological science with social, institutional, community, or environmental contexts. The successful candidate will advance an interdisciplinary agenda that explores both how policy shapes human behavior and how behavioral insights can optimize the design, evaluation, and translation of public interventions and policies. This joint appointment offers rich opportunities for collaboration across Psychology, Urban Planning and Public Policy, the School of Social Ecology, and the broader UC Irvine campus. Teaching and Mentoring The successful candidate will contribute to undergraduate and graduate teaching in Psychology and UPPP. Teaching may include courses addressing behavior change, decision-making, behavioral science, public policy, urban planning, and/or the candidate's substantive area of expertise. The candidate will mentor students across disciplinary boundaries and contribute to preparing students to apply psychological and behavioral science to complex social and policy problems. Position description The UCSF Department of Neurological Surgery and The Gladstone-UCSF Institute of Genomic Immunology are jointly recruiting a faculty member at the Assistant, Associate or Full Professor level to lead a new research program supported in part by the UCSF Brain Tumor Center, focused on immunotherapy for brain tumors. The successful candidate will be a basic scientist based at the Gladstone Institutes (Mission Bay), with primary faculty appointment in the Department of Neurological Surgery. Candidates must have a strong background in immunology, genomics, genetics, genome engineering, and/or synthetic biology, and significant achievements and meaningful promise in developing novel immunotherapies for brain tumors. We invite applications from scientists with Ph.D., M.D./Ph.D., or equivalent degrees who are establishing or have established an independent basic science research program in brain tumor immunotherapy research. Relevant areas of research include, but are not limited to: Genome engineering to enhance adoptive cellular therapies for brain cancer Protein design and engineering in the context of the immune system and immunotherapies for brain cancer Systems immunology and immunotherapy in neuro-oncology Preclinical disease models and clinical translation of innovative immunotherapies in the context of the brain Investigators will be expected to develop extramurally sponsored research programs and educate, mentor, and develop graduate and medical students. The successful candidate will hold a primary faculty appointment in the UCSF Department of Neurological Surgery, along with an Investigator affiliation at the Gladstone-UCSF Institute of Genomic Immunology, as an Assistant, Associate or Full Professor, and will be assigned dedicated research space, primarily located in new Gladstone Institutes space at Mission Bay, with additional support from the UCSF Brain Tumor Center. About Gladstone-UCSF Institute of Genomic Immunology To harness the immense potential offered by immunotherapies, the Gladstone-UCSF Institute of Genomic Immunology combines emerging biomedical technologies at the intersection of human immunology, genomics, CRISPR genome engineering, computational biology, and synthetic biology. The institute’s scientists deepen knowledge of how DNA sequences control cell functions in the human immune system. Their discoveries will enable the next generation of immunotherapies for cancer, autoimmune diseases, infectious diseases, inflammation and beyond. This institute is the result of a close partnership between Gladstone Institutes and the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF). With wet and dry lab space to be housed (starting in 2027) in a new building on the Mission Bay campus, it creates a unified community across the two campuses and combines UCSF’s world-class immunology and planned cell therapy efforts with Gladstone’s expertise in the host-pathogen interface, iPS cells, computational biology, and CRISPR gene editing technologies. Within our overarching advancing health worldwide mission, UCSF is devoted at every level to serving the public. Position description The School of Education (SOE) at the University of California, Davis, invites applications for a tenure-track, full-time assistant professor position with an opportunity for a joint affiliation with the UC Davis MIND Institute beginning Fall 2027. We seek applicants whose research and teaching offer transformative and critical insights into disability justice, neurodiversity and inclusion at the elementary and/or secondary level. We are especially interested in scholars who bring a design-based perspective to improving instructional practices, support structures, tools and technologies and organizational structures and who are committed to designing, testing and studying the implementation of programs and systems to improve learning opportunities for neurodivergent students of all backgrounds. The UC Davis School of Education is transforming education through the preparation of the best education leaders, researchers, and teachers in the country. We are committed to deepening our engagement in inclusive excellence by eliminating inequities in schooling and creating learning opportunities for diverse learners using the power of knowledge and the promise of education. The School of Education serves four programs: an undergraduate minor, credential and master's in Teacher Education, Ph.D., and the Capital Area North Doctorate in Educational Leadership (CANDEL) Ed.D. program. Position description The University of California, Davis, School of Medicine, Department of Emergency Medicine is recruiting two full-time research faculty members at the Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor level. Each position consists of a joint appointment in the Regular Series (50%) and In-Residence Series (50%). The anticipated start date is July 1, 2027. We seek investigators who will build independent, externally funded research programs and contribute to the Department’s missions in education, mentorship, service, and academic leadership. The Department is particularly interested in candidates with expertise in one or more of the following areas: Large database and population-based research, including causal inference, epidemiology, biostatistics, health services research, outcomes research, and analysis of large clinical or administrative datasets. Addiction medicine and substance use research, including opioid-related research and translational, clinical, public health, policy, implementation, or community-based approaches. Additional training through a formal postdoctoral fellowship or substantial prior research experience is preferred. Candidates should demonstrate potential for independent external funding at the Assistant Professor level or a sustained record of external funding at the Associate or Full Professor level. Successful candidates will be expected to develop and maintain active, externally funded research programs; engage in teaching, mentorship, and scholarly training of medical students, residents, fellows, and junior faculty; participate in departmental, university, and professional service activities; and contribute to the academic mission of the Department through research, education, leadership, and community engagement. The UC Davis Department of Emergency Medicine provides comprehensive emergency services to a large urban and referral population as a Level I Trauma Center, Comprehensive Stroke Center, and EMS base station. Position description Assistant Professor in Soil Science The Department of Environmental Sciences at the University of California, Riverside (UCR) invites applications for a tenure-track position in Soil Science at the rank of Assistant Professor on a nine-month appointment. The anticipated start date for this position is July 1, 2027. The successful candidate will develop a nationally and internationally recognized research program advancing fundamental and/or applied understanding of soils and their functions across agricultural, managed, and/or natural systems. We seek candidates whose research addresses soil processes across spatial and temporal scales and contributes to understanding the capacity of soils to support productive, resilient, and sustainable ecosystems. Areas of research may include, but are not limited to, soil health and resilience; soil biogeochemistry and nutrient cycling; soil-water interactions; soil carbon dynamics; soil responses to climate and land-use change; soil degradation and restoration; and the effects of soil management on ecosystem function. Soil health in degraded, arid, and semi-arid landscapes and agroecosystems, including those of the U.S. Southwest, represents one example of an important and developing area of soil science. Research may span agricultural and natural systems and may employ field, laboratory, computational, geospatial, or other approaches across scales. Applicants that integrate themes of sustainability in connection to their research and other scholarly work are encouraged to apply. The UCR Department of Environmental Sciences is distinguished by its deep historical roots in soil and water sciences, its top-ranked interdisciplinary research in atmospheric and environmental chemistry, and its vital impact on solving critical regional climate and sustainability challenges. The incumbent will be encouraged to collaborate with current faculty in related fields including agricultural water and land management, agronomy, precision agriculture, atmospheric science, biogeochemistry and isotope biogeochemistry, ecosystem sciences, environmental microbiology/soil biology, environmental chemistry/toxicology, geomorphology, and hydrology. The successful candidate will also contribute to advancing the sustainability of California’s agricultural and/or natural resource systems through mission-oriented research and outreach aligned with the goals of UCR’s Agricultural Experiment Station. The candidate will be expected to develop and disseminate research-based knowledge and engage with relevant audiences to translate scientific advances into benefits for California and society. The successful candidate is expected to engage fully in the teaching mission of the Department and University, including formal classroom instruction in the Environmental Sciences undergraduate and graduate degree programs and mentoring of undergraduate, M.S., and Ph.D. students. The successful candidate will be expected to contribute to the Environmental Sciences curricula, and/or to future programs and curricula in agricultural sciences, hydrology, and sustainability that may be (co-) administered by the Environmental Sciences Department. The teaching load will include a core undergraduate course for the Environmental Sciences major

Position description In-Residence Faculty Position – Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor Department of Pharmaceutical Chemistry University of California, San Francisco The UCSF Department of Pharmaceutical Chemistry in conjunction with the Cardiovascular Research Institute (CVRI) seeks faculty active in synthetic chemistry and/or chemical biology to join our vibrant, collaborative, and supportive discovery research community at the Mission Bay Campus in San Francisco. The Department of Pharmaceutical Chemistry includes diverse research in the areas of computational and synthetic chemistry, biophysics, chemical biology, peptide and protein design, systems and synthetic biology, enabling technologies, and drug discovery. Our department is characterized by a culture of collaboration and innovation in biomedical science: Faculty members typically have positions in one or more of our graduate groups (e.g., Chemistry & Chemical Biology, Biophysics & Computational Biology). Many of our faculty have positions in one or more institutes, which provide opportunities for additional collaborations and resources. The CVRI is devoted to fundamental research with direct or indirect relevance to cardiovascular disease. We seek creative, innovative scientists who define and address fundamental questions in chemical biology. We are particularly interested in chemists, who wish to build a program that blends organic synthesis with biochemical, computational, and analytical methods to probe biological mechanisms. We provide faculty with resources to launch their program, including a strong mentoring culture, a competitive start-up package, administrative support, and facilities for advanced computation, organic synthesis, light and cryo-electron microscopy, mass spectrometry, high-throughput small molecule screening, cytometry, and state-of-the-art animal care. Our available lab space is well equipped for organic synthesis, cell biological, and biochemical research. We encourage those at all levels of their careers to apply. Faculty candidates are expected to hold a Ph.D., to have demonstrated substantial research accomplishment and potential, and to be committed to the mentorship of students in research. Faculty appointment will be made at a professorial rank commensurate with current academic standing. UCSF offers competitive salaries, research set-up funds, and recruitment allowances, and has numerous opportunities for faculty development and further training in mentorship. The total compensation for this position ranges from $126,800-$332,700. jobs.description: Position overview Position title: Post-Doctoral Researcher Salary range: TBD Review timeline: September 15, 2026 Application Window Open date: September 15, 2026 Next review date: Friday, Nov 13, 2026 at 11:59pm (Pacific Time) Apply by this date to ensure full consideration by the committee. Position description The UCLA CMRS Center for Early Global Studies is pleased to announce a John W. Baldwin Post-Doctoral Fellowship for a recent Ph.D. whose work focuses on European medieval studies within the global comparative context. The position is for a maximum of 2 years, beginning July 1, 2027. To be eligible for consideration, applicants must have received their Ph.D. between September 1, 2020, and June 30, 2027. The Post-Doctoral Fellow will be a scholar whose research aligns with the goals of the study of “Europe in the world” and who has demonstrated evidence of innovative methodologies. A successful applicant may be working in a discipline or between disciplines in the European Middle Ages but should engage Europe in the world at micro and macro levels. We understand the European Middle Ages to include the period from the 3rd to the start of the 17th century, and where the 16th century is studied in continuity with the late medieval period. Mirroring the work of John W. Baldwin, for whom the postdoctoral fellowship is named, a successful applicant will conceive of Europe within a broader global context and be conversant across disciplines. The Fellow will join the vibrant research and academic communities within the CMRS Center for Early Global Studies, with scholars working on all facets of early Global studies. He/she/they will have the following responsibilities and opportunities: develop their research agenda while participating regularly in CMRS-CEGS academic events; work collaboratively with a diverse group of scholars, graduate students, and other postdoctoral fellows; help to conceive Center’s programming (including public-facing programming). He/she/they will have the opportunity to prepare one scholarly event (workshop or small symposium) hosted by CMRS-CEGS in the second year. Named to honor the legacy of the esteemed historian JOHN W. BALDWIN, this postdoctoral fellowship is made possible by a gift from Arcadia, a charitable fund that works to protect nature, preserve cultural heritage and promote open access to knowledge. Position description The Environmental Markets Lab (emLab) is seeking a postdoctoral researcher to lead in the design and on-the-water pilot of market-based conservation mechanisms, such as payments for ecosystem services, to reduce catch of endangered species (turtles, sharks, and other sensitive species) by fisheries in the Eastern Tropical Pacific Ocean. Work will be completed in collaboration with emLab Directors, along with Conservation International’s (CI) field teams, local management agencies, and fishers in Latin America. This position is part of the UCSB-CI Arnhold Climate Solutions Collaborative, a partnership focused on conducting cutting-edge applied research and developing tangible, progressive solutions. The Environmental Markets Lab (emLab) is a team of scientists based at UC Santa Barbara that advances economic research to deliver practical solutions for people and the planet. In collaboration with implementing partners, we design, test, and implement scalable solutions that work across boundaries—connecting science with policy, data with decisions, and ambition with action—to create pathways toward a future where environmental and human well being mutually reinforce one another. We endeavor to foster an inclusive, collaborative work environment to bring interdisciplinary expertise to solve critical environmental problems. The postdoctoral researcher will work with emLab and can also allocate a fraction of their time to their own research. The postdoc would join an ongoing NIH-funded project on using NLP, LLMs, dialogue, and speech processing to analyze clinical language data in order to better understand pragmatic and social language difficulties in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and Fragile X syndrome (FXS) and potential genetic contributors. The postdoc would be mentored by Rob Voigt and be part of a large interdisciplinary team at UC Davis and Northwestern University including Co-PI Molly Losh. The team includes researchers in NLP, linguistics, and communication sciences and disorders with deep technical and domain expertise, and works collaboratively across the UC Davis Linguistic Mechanisms Lab (Voigt) and the Northwestern Neurodevelopmental Disabilities Lab (Losh). Together these are fun, supportive, and collaborative groups providing many opportunities for learning, hands-on research and teamwork. Candidates should have a PhD in Linguistics, Computer Science, or a related field with a strong technical background in NLP and LLMs. Interest and/or experience in working with dialogue, speech, or clinical data are preferred, as is theoretical background in pragmatics or sociolinguistics. A significant portion of the project includes multilingual comparisons between English and Mandarin Chinese, so fluency in Mandarin or with multilingual computational modelling are significant benefits as well. The project encompasses a wide variety of research areas and methods, including modeling conversational interaction and dialogue structure, developing metrics for pragmatic and social language understanding, cross-lingual comparison, and could also include speech processing. Position description The University of California, Santa Barbara seeks a highly motivated postdoctoral scholar to lead a new research program examining how wildlife communities respond to the rapidly expanding wildland-urban interface. As development increasingly borders and fragments natural habitat, an important set of ecological and conservation questions is emerging: How do animal communities change across the transition from relatively intact wildlands to developed landscapes? Which species tolerate or exploit edges, and which are displaced by them? Do protected lands adjacent to development function as refuges, foraging habitat, or movement corridors? How do human-associated resources alter wildlife behavior and food webs? Can strategically-protected habitat at the wildland-urban boundary help sustain ecological communities while reducing negative interactions between wildlife and people? This research will address these questions in the Santa Barbara foothills surrounding Los Padres National Forest, an area of mountain wildlands abutting developed coastal landscapes. Specific research questions will be developed collaboratively with the successful candidate, who will have substantial intellectual freedom to shape the scientific direction of the project. Example research questions may include: ● How do vertebrate species richness, community composition, and activity change across gradients of human development? ● Which species are most sensitive to wildland-urban edges, and which species benefit from or tolerate them? ● Does wildlife activity become increasingly nocturnal near residences and other human activity? ● How do responses to development differ among mammals, birds, bats, amphibians, and other vertebrate groups? ● How do wildlife responses to developed edges change seasonally or during periods of drought and resource limitation? ● Do protected areas at the wildland-urban boundary function primarily as habitat, refuge, foraging areas, or movement corridors? ● How does proximity to development alter wildlife diets and trophic interactions? ● When and why do wildlife begin relying on human-associated foods, ornamental vegetation, commensal prey, or other anthropogenic resources? ● More broadly, what characteristics make protected lands at the wildland-urban interface most effective at maintaining biodiversity and ecological function? The project will be designed to integrate multiple complementary approaches. jobs.title: Postdoctoral Scholar in Fusion Simulation
jobs.description: Position overview Salary range: Starting $71,491 Review timeline: For full consideration in the first review of applicants, materials should be submitted by November 30, 2026. Application Window Open date: October 19, 2026 Next review date: Monday, Nov 30, 2026 at 11:59pm (Pacific Time) Apply by this date to ensure full consideration by the committee. Final date: Sunday, Jan 31, 2027 at 11:59pm (Pacific Time) Applications will continue to be accepted until this date, but those received after the review date will only be considered if the position has not yet been filled. Position description Fusion Energy represents one of the grand challenges for humankind, offering the prospect of limitless baseload electricity, an inherently safe configuration, with no significant greenhouse gases or nuclear waste. As a thriving fusion industry develops multiple promising concepts for fusion, it is vital to look ahead to solutions for continuous energy production. Thus, UCLA seeks to pioneer the steady state tokamak as a concept in its own right, and as a tensioner to drive the development of the many constituent science and engineering components of the challenge, that will drive broader benefits to the fusion field. To this end, UCLA is establishing a Fusion Simulation Center to develop concepts for a compact fusion power plant that integrates foundational discovery plasma science, fusion science and engineering. The explicit goal is the development of robust and cost-effective configurations overall for fusion in steady state, as well as innovative approaches and advanced solutions in each of the technical fields and systems comprising a power plant. This work will thus serve as an integrating focus of a very broad range of activities across Engineering and Science at UCLA from energy extraction, blanket design, tritium breeding, and materials development to fundamental plasma science and efficient energy-confining plasma configurations. Thus, the Department of Physics & Astronomy at UCLA seeks outstanding candidates as a postdoctoral scholar in the area of Fusion Simulation. Key responsibilities and tasks will include: Using simulation suites to develop optimized configurations for fusion power plants or other fusion testbed devices. Writing software modules to address specific facets of this challenge. Undertaking investigations into particular aspects of the power plant solutions (could range from fundamental discovery or fusion plasma science questions to technology aspects such as facets of blanket design or materials behavior, depending on skill of applicant. Support to other users as needed, including students and student projects in the center. Generate scientific deliverables including journal papers and conference talks. Pursuing collaborative engagement within UCLA and or other key partners to investigate particular issues and approaches. Potentially to engage in, or collaborate with validation exercises such as experimental tests on tokamaks or other testbed devices. The successful candidate is expected to be able to operate with autonomy and grapple with highly complex technical issues, distilling them down to essential understanding for a working knowledge. Qualified candidates will have a Ph.D. in Physics or a related field, 3+ years experience and a demonstrated background directly applicable to the tasks, including experience with fusion simulation activities on the science or engineering side. Specific understanding of relevant plasma science or fusion technology is essential, but may be weighted to the plasma science and/or fusion technology side. Candidates should provide a curriculum vitae; a publication list; a Statement of Research Interests and Future Research Goals, complete a reference check authorization release form, and arrange for 2-3 letters of reference to be uploaded to UCLA Academic Recruit by November 30. Qualifications Basic qualifications Ph.D. in plasma physics or a closely related fusion technology

Position description The Aggarwal Group at UC Davis is looking for a postdoc to play a leading role in R&D toward a new tabletop radio-frequency gravitational wave detector, targeting the axion, a leading dark matter candidate. Axions can form clouds around black holes through superradiance, and those clouds emit gravitational waves. The detector concept is a Fabry-Perot Michelson interferometer with an optically trapped micro-disk in each arm cavity. It is also a promising platform for sub-SQL techniques such as sensing with squeezed light. You will work under the supervision of Prof. Aggarwal and in close collaboration with Prof. Andrew Geraci’s group at Northwestern, which is developing a companion detector, with the goal of running the two jointly. Some travel to Chicago may be needed, depending on the experiment. This position is supported by a new DOE award for R&D on hybrid quantum sensing schemes using optical levitation and interferometry. The initial appointment is two years, renewable annually subject to mutual satisfaction, and the award covers the full initial appointment. Training at LIGO. Interested candidates can spend extended periods at the LIGO observatories to learn commissioning techniques. These techniques are directly useful for the R&D on this project. The Group. We develop instrumentation for precision measurements, with a focus on ultralight dark matter and gravitational wave searches. The group is also involved in ARIADNE, a search for short-range spin-dependent forces mediated by the QCD axion, and in the LIGO collaboration, where we search for dark matter using LIGO instruments and data. ~*~ How to Apply Apply online at Browse Open Recruitments or Log In - AP Recruit. Position description POSITION SUMMARY The Sparks Laboratory seeks a motivated Postdoctoral Scholar to investigate the molecular and epigenetic mechanisms that regulate early human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC) differentiation. The scholar will contribute to an NIGMS MIRA/R35 research program focused on neural crest (NC) and mesoderm (meso) lineage specification, with particular emphasis on DNA methylation, microRNA (miRNA) regulation, gene expression, and chromatin accessibility. The research integrates stem cell biology, developmental biology, molecular and cellular assays, and multi-omics approaches to define intermediate cell states and regulatory mechanisms during early differentiation. The position is designed for a scholar interested in developing an independent research profile while working collaboratively on mechanistic studies of human development. Opportunities will include experimental design, generation and integration of genomic datasets, functional validation of candidate regulators, manuscript preparation, scientific presentations, and development of future research directions. Position description The Sue & Bill Gross School of Nursing is currently accepting applications for temporary Unit 18 Lecturers (Non-Senate Faculty) to teach core clinical and non-clinical courses in the Doctor of Nursing Practice- Family Nurse Practitioner Program. These lecturer appointments will initially be made on a quarterly basis in the School of Nursing, with potential for continuing employment. Salary is commensurate with experience and at varying percentages of time, depending on the number and nature of courses assigned. REQUIREMENTS FOR THE POSITION: The School is looking for dynamic and collaborative educators who have shown an established track record for developing high-quality graduate-level curriculum designed for online, synchronous and asynchronous delivery. Candidates are required to have previous experience teaching DNP-FNP courses and/or similar courses in the University of California system and/or an equivalent education setting. Information about the School of Nursing can be found at: UC Irvine Sue & Bill Gross School of Nursing – Nursing With Humanity in Mind ABOUT THE SUE & BILL GROSS SCHOOL OF NURSING The Sue & Bill Gross School of Nursing at UC Irvine is the newest nursing school in the prestigious University of California system and the only nursing school in the UC system with a faculty practice. The Sue & Bill Gross School of Nursing is leading the way. Firmly committed to inclusive excellence, we are preparing nurse scholars who advance the science that guides practice, and we are preparing future faculty and policy specialists who educate our students to address the growing, aging and increasingly diverse population of California and the nation. The academic programs that the Sue & Bill Gross School of Nursing offers educate nursing professionals of tomorrow to excel in clinical or research settings. Since 2007, our program has had an astonishing 100 percent pass rate on National Nurse Practitioner Board Certified exams. Academic degrees offered include a Bachelor of Science in Nursing Science, a Master of Science in Nursing Science, a Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) degree, with or without a Family Nurse Practitioner concentration (DNP-FNP); and a Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Nursing Science. The School of Nursing is one of four academic units in the College of Health Sciences which includes a School of Medicine, School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Science and Programs in Public Health.
